currentImplementation.contractPrecondition: backend workingSetBytes is a conservative total peak for the complete probe/request execution, not merely codec-private scratch bytes
hostPostDecodeChecks: decoded dimensions and pixel count remain inside DecodeLimits
decoded dimensions do not exceed the requested target box
actual CGImage resident byte cost does not exceed the admitted complete-frame working-set bytes
decoded source-profile fact matches the validated probe source-profile fact

postDecodeChecks: single returned image resident bytes <= configured host hard limit
progressiveStatus.preDecodePeakAdmission: open: current ImageProgressiveDecodeSession contract exposes no per-session or per-generation resource estimate

interpretation.maxReportedTotals: Safe only under the current contract precondition that each backend report is already a conservative total peak for the full decode execution. The disjoint/partial-overlap counterexamples demonstrate why max is unsound if a future contract reinterprets backendBytes as codec-private scratch.
interpretation.nextContractTrigger: If future codecs cannot conservatively express one total peak, evolve ImageCraftCore to versioned phase/coverage resource envelopes rather than summing or maxing ambiguous reports.
interpretation.postDecodeValidation: Catches returned-object contract violations and some estimate under-reporting, but cannot retroactively prevent a transient codec scratch peak that already occurred during decode.
